title: Competitive signal decomposition to product levers playbook
creator: Elena Morris
description:
Objective: Turn raw competitive signals (model feature announcements, pricing shifts, latency/throughput benchmarks, quantization claims, and outage events) into an operational mapping that directly recommends product levers (routing policy, fallback model choices, caching rules, quantization profiles, pricing tiers, and rollout cadence).

Scope:
- Ingest signal feeds (public releases, vendor pricing updates, telemetry from internal benchmarks, customer-reported regressions).
- Define a taxonomy of signals and map each to 1..n product levers with estimated impact and confidence.
- Produce a lightweight decision canvas that PMs/SEs can use to choose immediate mitigations (e.g., switch to low-latency variant, enable prefix cache, adjust rate limits) and medium-term investments (dedicated capacity procurement, quantization support, policy-driven fallbacks).

Success metrics:
- Triage-to-action latency: <72h for high-severity signals.
- Reduction in customer-experienced outage-time due to model supply incidents by 30% within 3 months of adoption.
- Playbook adoption: used in at least 3 incident responses and 5 roadmap decisions in Q2.

Data sources and instrumentation required:
- External: vendor release feeds (RSS + curated Slack channel), model-compatibility trackers (internal), public benchmarks.
- Internal: per-model latency/cost dashboards (console dashboards), error/timeout SLO traces, customer tickets tagged with model provider.
- Quick telemetry extraction tickets created: ENG-50211 (latency histogram API), ENG-50212 (per-tenant fallback rates).

Initial hypothesis and findings from reconnaissance:
- Many vendor claims (quantized throughput improvements) only hold at long sequence lengths; short conversations see smaller wins. This pushes us toward a routing lever rather than blanket quantization.
- Customers in search-heavy verticals trade embedding cost for latency; a price-tiered routing policy (cheap-embedding for batch analytics vs fast-embedding for real-time) is a high-leverage product lever.
- Outages for a single vendor correlate with immediate upticks in request errors in specific regions; region-aware fallback + cached prefix reduces immediate impact.

High-level decomposition matrix (excerpt):
- Signal: Vendor price cut on tokens -> Levers: pricing tier adjustments, model-routing to cheaper model variants, customer notifications. Impact: cost. Confidence: medium. Trade-offs: short-term margin pressure vs retention.
- Signal: New quantized variant with 2x throughput claims -> Levers: pilot on Dedicated pools, measure real-world throughput, recommend per-workload quantization profiles. Impact: latency/cost. Confidence: low->medium.

Decisions made:
- Focus initial playbook on 3 levers: routing policies, caching rules (prefix & KV), and quantization pilot gating. Remove 'automatic pricing changes' from scope for now; pricing changes will be a separate GTM/finance-led project.
- Use a three-tier severity model for signal urgency (Critical: outage/regression affecting customers; High: pricing/latency shift with measurable telemetry; Medium: new model features).

Open trade-offs and risks:
- Automating routing decisions risks oscillation and model thrash. Plan: start with a human-in-the-loop mode and conservative cooldown windows.
- Relying on vendor-provided microbenchmarks is dangerous; we must instrument in-prod-like workloads (task: PM-655321 synthetic-customer-workload-lab).

Deliverables:
1) Playbook doc + decision canvas (Confluence) with worked examples.
2) A small reference runbook used in two incident drills.
3) Mapping artifact exported as JSON schema for Console (for future UI integration).

Next steps (owners):
- PM (Ravi): draft playbook + worked examples by 2026-03-20.
- Research lead (Elena): complete 6 vendor signoff interviews and capture quotes by 2026-03-18.
- Eng (assigned): telemetry endpoints (ENG-50211, ENG-50212) - ETA 2 sprints.
- Design: build a compact decision canvas wireframe (link in Links) and a version for incident runbooks.

Notes & sample interview excerpts:
- "We saw a 20% latency drop on batched workloads, but tail latency for interactive traffic did not improve." 20	4 Platform engineer, OEM vendor (interview 2026-03-05).
- "If routing to a cheaper model means removing advanced safety filters, our compliance team will block it." 20	4 Enterprise customer security lead (2026-03-07).

Attachments and artifacts: see Links.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook published in Confluence with at least 3 real worked examples and an attached JSON mapping file.
- Two incident drills performed using the playbook with after-action summaries.

Longer-term: integrate with Console to surface suggested levers when a signal is detected (UI card + one-click recommended action).
